phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: The paper examines how a 2017-2018 precipitation whiplash (pluvial to drought) fuelled spring wildfires in the Southern Great Plains, with their impacts (acres burned, fatalities, homes).
phase_a_scope.reader_2_reason: The paper examines how a 2017-2018 wet-to-dry precipitation whiplash and drought related to wildfire numbers and acres burned in the Southern Great Plains.

phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: The paper quantifies summer heat exposure (modelled air-temperature metrics) at US prisons and its relation to population and facility characteristics; heat hazard, exposure and vulnerability are the subject.
phase_a_scope.reader_2_reason: The paper examines summer heat exposure at US prisons using modeled air temperature, and how exposure differs by population and facility characteristics.

evidence.evidence_text: Across all prisons, the population-weighted summer heat exposure for the white, non-Hispanic, Black, non-Hispanic, American Indian non-Hispanic, Asian, non-Hispanic, and non-white, non-Hispanic incarcerated populations was between 93.2 and 94.7°F, while the Hispanic or Latino subgroup had the highest population-weighted exposure at 97.1°F (Table S4 in Supporting Information S1).

reader_2_only.text: Based on the 90th percentile summer air temperature, the most heat-exposed prisons, and the states with the highest average prison heat exposure, were mostly in the Southwestern US.

evidence.evidence_text: With regards to the patterns of the 90th percentile summer air temperature, we found that the most heat-exposed facilities and the states with the highest prison heat exposures on average were mostly in the Southwestern US where there are not universal air conditioning regulations in prisons (Santucci et al., 2022).

reader_2_only.text: The highest facility-level temperature anomalies in 2020-2023, relative to a historical baseline, occurred at prisons in the Pacific Northwest, the Northeast, Texas, and parts of the Midwest.

evidence.evidence_text: With this approach, we found that the highest facility-level temperature anomalies from 2020 to 2023 occurred in the Pacific Northwest, the Northeast, Texas, and parts of the Midwest.

reader_2_only.text: In 2019, the 10 most heat-exposed prisons had 15.0% higher proportions of Hispanic or Latino incarcerated people than the 10 least heat-exposed prisons.

evidence.evidence_text: The prisons with the top 10 heat exposures also had 15.0% higher proportions of Hispanic or Latino incarcerated populations than the lowest 10 prisons (Figure 4).

phase_c_statistics.caveat: n is small (4 items, 13 aligned pairs). Descriptive counts of two readings of a relevance-guided sample, not estimates of reader reliability; no inferential statement.
